newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume surges to 1.3 T on demand.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume surges to 1.3 T on demand.

text.p: Traded volume on Istanbul's gold exchange more than tripled to 1,300 kilos on Friday amid free market demand buoyed by expectations of upward ounce prices and of a weaker lira in the domestic currency markets, dealers said.
Gold dived to $380.35 an ounce from Thursday's $383.25 close and to 1,212,850 lira from 1,215,500 in line with world trends.

Dealers said the price drop in lira terms was less as the lira weakened against the dollar on persisting bank demand for the U.S. currency in the domestic market. It closed at 98,730 to the dollar versus 98,525 on Thursday.

"Upward price expectations in world gold markets, taking new positions after gold sales at $383 levels earlier in the week and expectations that the dollar will remain strong in the local currency market fuelled purchases," said a free market dealer.

Some 630 kilos of gold traded in the first session and 670 in the afternoon with Monday value as buyers sought to replace gold to be sold over the weekend. 69 percent of the total turnover was conducted in lira terms. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
